clue.text: There's some cost in involving financial experts

indicators.note: involving is read as twisting together, so these three words are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes that bringing in economists always costs money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' signals the anagram: SOME COST IN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Economists are specialists who study money, trade and finance.

clue.text: Edited diaries involve Liberal PM

indicators.note: involve means take in, so the rearranged letters wrap around the abbreviation
edited text has been reworked, so the letters of this word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Liberal prime minister's diaries have been edited for publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edited' turns DIARIES into DISRAEI, and 'involve' takes L inside it. The surface says 'Liberal PM', but Disraeli was a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was twice British prime minister in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Presents for volunteers

definitions.meaning: as a verb, presents means puts forward or proffers
as a verb, volunteers means puts oneself or something forward unasked

explanation.definitionFit: To offer is both to present something and to volunteer it.

clue.text: Dutch half-sovereign

parts.note: not a coin: the queen who shared the English throne equally with her Dutch husband William of Orange

explanation.surface: Sounds like an old Dutch coin worth half a sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-sovereign is a British gold coin, which is the false trail. Mary II reigned jointly with the Dutch William III, so she was half of a sovereign pair, and a Dutch queen by marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Mary II co-reigned with William of Orange, holding half the joint monarchy.

clue.text: Newly written aria to man's loved ones

indicators.note: something newly written has been recomposed, so these letters are set in a new order

parts.note: the word man's supplies its four letters including the S

explanation.surface: A composer writes a fresh aria for a man's sweethearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly written' signals the anagram of ARIA TO MANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inamoratas are women who are loved, sweethearts or mistresses.

clue.text: Meat loaf put out for picnic

indicators.note: the loaf is put out round the meat, stretched to enclose it

parts.note: a loaf can be a cake, as in a loaf cake
lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: A meat loaf is set out on the rug for an outdoor meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' means the cake is extended around LAMB, giving C-LAMB-AKE. A clambake is an American seaside party where clams are cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A clambake is an outdoor seaside feast, a kind of picnic.

clue.text: Find company in one churchman or another

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the clergyman

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman finds friends among the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one churchman' is the DEAN, and the definition 'another' means a different churchman, so the deacon is defined by the clue's own words.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is a further rank of churchman, below a priest.

clue.text: Grudging admiration of diplomat who lacks nothing

indicators.note: lacks means goes without, so the zero letter is removed from the diplomat

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomat
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A penniless diplomat looks at others with resentful admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is resentful desire for what another has, admiration tinged with grudge.

clue.text: One newt in file is the leader

indicators.note: in places the two short pieces inside the line

parts.note: a file or line of things in a row can be a chain
one is the Roman numeral I
an eft is a newt, especially a young one

explanation.surface: A newt in a queue is put at the front of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One newt' reads as a single amphibian, but splits into the numeral and the young-newt word, an old term common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the head of a clan or tribe, its leader.

clue.text: Rise late — about one will be right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the legal claim goes round the numeral

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A late riser claims it is their right to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: LIEN goes round I to make LIE-I-N.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-in is staying in bed late in the morning; the verb phrase means to rise late.

clue.text: Two-year-olds run in it — in two ways perhaps

definitions.text: Two-year-olds run in it — in two ways perhaps

parts.words: Two-year-olds run in it — in two ways perhaps
parts.note: toddlers run about in a children's room, and two-year-old racehorses run in a race restricted to their age

explanation.surface: Two-year-olds romp about there, whether children or horses.
explanation.walkthrough: A nursery is a playroom for small children, and in horse racing a nursery is a handicap race for two-year-olds.
explanation.definitionFit: Both toddlers' playrooms and races for juvenile horses share this name.

clue.text: Mockery makes Bohemian girl weep

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème
to weep is to cry

explanation.surface: A girl from Bohemia is reduced to tears by teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimicry is imitation, often in mockery of the person copied.

clue.text: Hunts with seeming success

parts.note: gatherings of a fox hunt have a name, and the same word followed by 'with success' means achieves it

explanation.surface: Fox hunts that appear to go well.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunt's gatherings are its meets; 'meets with success' means succeeds, which the clue twists.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunt meets, and its assemblies are called meets; one meets with success.

clue.text: Start to play

parts.note: the moment a theatre performance begins, when the drapes rise

explanation.surface: Begin playing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to play' reads as 'begin to play', but it means the start of a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtain-up is the rise of the stage curtain marking a show's beginning.

clue.text: Final move for vice-consul

indicators.note: a move shifts things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vice-consul makes a decisive last move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' signals the anagram of VICECONSUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Conclusive means decisive and settling the matter, hence final.

clue.text: One without a car needs a trip out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Someone who has no car must walk if they want an outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals the anagram of NEEDS A TRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestrian is someone travelling on foot rather than in a vehicle.

clue.text: Evading duty?

parts.note: slang for shirking work by faking illness, from a sailor taking soundings with a weighted line, an easy task

explanation.surface: Dodging work or avoiding tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty' suggests customs duty, but the sense is work. The phrase is British slang for malingering.
explanation.definitionFit: Swinging the lead is an idiom for shirking work by pretending to be ill.

clue.text: Biblical swine are eager and wild

definitions.note: the definition is the phrase naming the herd; the answer is the adjective attached to that herd

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so these letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Pigs in the Bible are keen and untamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' signals the anagram of EAGER AND; 'are' is a link. In the Gospels, demons driven into pigs at Gadara sent them rushing into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gadarene swine are the possessed pigs of the Gospel story, so the adjective identifies them.

clue.text: Insect with wings of short span

definitions.text: Insect with wings of short span

parts.words: Insect with wings of short span
parts.note: the mayfly genus, whose winged adults live only a day; also things of brief life

explanation.surface: A winged insect with a short wingspan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'span' suggests wingspan, but the short span is of life: mayflies live about a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera is the mayfly genus and also means short-lived things.

clue.text: Takes an attitude over something that's beneath you

definitions.text: Takes an attitude over something that's beneath you

parts.words: Takes an attitude over something that's beneath you
parts.note: physically, sits or stands with a leg either side of something below; figuratively, sits on the fence over an issue

explanation.surface: Acts superior about something beneath one's dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beneath you' suggests disdain, but it means literally under your legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle is to stand astride something, and also to take an equivocal position.

clue.text: Sound wave

definitions.meaning: a sound, as in a light murmur of applause or laughter

explanation.definitionFit: A ripple is a gentle murmur of sound and also a small wavelet.

clue.text: Remains of pitched battles

definitions.meaning: the England-Australia cricket test series, fought on a pitch

explanation.walkthrough: THE ASHES is the cricket series between England and Australia, played on a pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are burnt remains, and the Ashes is a famous cricket contest.

clue.text: The voice of the doer

parts.note: in grammar, the verb form where the subject performs the action

explanation.surface: Someone who gets things done speaks up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'voice' is the grammatical term: in 'the dog bit him' the subject is the doer.
explanation.definitionFit: The active voice is the verb form in which the subject performs the action.

clue.text: They get taken in by foreigners

definitions.text: They get taken in by foreigners

parts.words: They get taken in by foreigners
parts.note: goods sent abroad are received by other countries, not deceived ones

explanation.surface: People who are duped by those from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests deceived, but it means received.
explanation.definitionFit: Exports are goods shipped abroad, which overseas buyers take in.

clue.text: She has them shortened to a degree

indicators.note: shortened means clipped, as in the casual form that drops the opening letters

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A woman has some items taken up to the right length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' turns THEM into the informal 'EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a woman's name, so it fits 'she'.

clue.text: Send a pound back for English martyr

indicators.note: back means the whole sequence is read from the end

parts.note: to remit is to send money
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Asked to send a pound back to commemorate an English martyr.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REMIT A L into LATIMER. Hugh Latimer was a Protestant bishop burnt at Oxford in 1555.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugh Latimer was an English bishop burnt at the stake for his Protestant faith.

clue.text: Novice leads expert in tie

indicators.note: leads means comes in front of

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A beginner leads an expert in a tied match.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L-plate, so L means novice.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace is to tie, as with shoelaces.

clue.text: The Italian man about town

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the man goes round the article

parts.note: taken as written
il is Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: An Italian man about town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man about town' looks like a set phrase for a socialite, but it splits: the definition is just 'town'.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan is a large city in northern Italy; 'town' is used loosely.

clue.text: Eve's vicar is upset when the order's changed

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the word Eve's supplies its four letters including the S

explanation.surface: The vicar's wife Eve is upset when the service order changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is upset' signals the anagram of EVES VICAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice versa means the other way round, with the order reversed.
